title: 3 things we noticed about Kesko's next 12 months

blocks.front: Dahl, a rights issue, five warehouses: busy year
blocks.back: Hi Kesko team. Congrats on the European Commission clearance for Dahl. With the Dahl integration, the rights issue and the warehouse rollout all landing together, we wondered which handoffs still depend on people re-keying data. Would it be worth a quick call to compare notes? - [Velho founder]

blocks.text: Kesko is in a busy stretch: a large Nordic acquisition, a planned capital raise, and a warehouse platform rollout all land within the same year. Here is what we noticed from public sources, and what we would want to ask.
1. The Dahl integration is a big reconciliation job

items.text: Kesko agreed to acquire Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark for a debt-free price of €1.2bn, with completion targeted by end-2026.
The European Commission unconditionally approved the deal; completion still depends on other conditions.

blocks.text: Dahl keeps separate brands and units. We noticed that this can mean order and financial data reconciled across several systems during integration. We have not seen how Kesko is handling this, so it is a question, not a diagnosis.
Inferred from the deal structure, not from any internal Kesko information.
2. Capital raise and efficiency focus arrive together

items.text: Kesko plans a €500-700m rights issue to refinance part of the bridge financing; an EGM on 2026-10-30 would authorise it. Terms are not yet set.
Q2 2026 comparable operating profit rose to €194m; full-year guidance narrowed to €670-730m.

blocks.text: Capital discipline and a margin focus usually make post-deal efficiency work a priority. The Q3 report on 29 October is a natural point where management may say what comes first.

blocks.label: Why now
blocks.why: Deal completion, EGM and Q3 results all fall within a few months.

blocks.text: 3. The warehouse stack is being rebuilt

items.text: Kesko selected Manhattan Associates' ActiveWarehouse cloud solution; the initial rollout covers five distribution centres, with a new site planned for 2029-30.

blocks.text: A new core platform often leaves gaps around it: integrations, exception handling and handoffs that still run on spreadsheets or people. We would ask where those gaps sit before assuming anything.

rows: Which order and finance flows from Dahl will need manual reconciliation?
Integration timing is set by end-2026
What sits outside the warehouse platform today?
Where does post-capital-raise spending go first?
Depends on EGM and Q3 results

blocks.label: Email
blocks.text:
Hi Jorma,

We noticed Kesko has a lot moving at once: the Dahl integration, the rights issue and the warehouse rollout. We would be curious whether any of the handoffs between those systems still rely on manual work.

We would be glad to share a short, free look at where that time goes. No pitch, just a 20-minute call if it is useful.

Best,
[Velho team member]
